summary: Nostr-first SoulFactory OpenClaw MVP app startup wiring behind explicit disabled-by-default config.
observed_context: docs/plans/soulfactory-openclaw-mvp-orchestration.md Item 1 requires Beads/PSTF skeleton, additive disabled config, app construction wiring, and deterministic disabled/enabled/invalid config tests.
internal/soulfactory contains an event-driven reactor, FullProvisioner, Signet-backed signer interface, and OpenClaw runtime-control adapter.
internal/app/app.go previously imported SoulFactory only for operator-assistant bootstrap and did not register a SoulFactory app reactor.
intended_behavior: SoulFactory remains Nostr-first and app startup does not add REST provisioning or lifecycle routes.
soul_factory configuration is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled with relays, authorized requester pubkeys, Signet bunker URI, and LLM settings.
When enabled with valid config, Bahia constructs a real Signet-backed SoulFactory reactor, FullProvisioner, and OpenClaw runtime adapter and registers the reactor as a background runner.
When disabled, Bahia constructs no SoulFactory Signet client, runtime adapter, reactor, or runner.
Invalid enabled config fails deterministically before production signer/runtime construction.
out_of_scope: Item 2 publication hardening and Bahia projection changes.
Item 3 workspace/client/web alignment beyond documentation of app-level config.
Fake OpenClaw deployment artifacts or synthetic deployable image digests.
